hints: Now count node pairs whose distance lies in [k1,k2].
At a centroid, collect the distances of nodes in each child subtree.
Use sorted distance lists or frequency prefix sums to count pairs within the range, subtracting same-subtree pairs before recursing.
analogy: At a centroid, count pairs that pass through it, then recurse into each piece for pairs that do not.
example: If two branches contain depths 1 and 3 and the allowed range is 3..4, their distance 4 contributes one pair.
algorithm: Use centroid decomposition. At each centroid, combine depth counts from different subtrees to count sums in [k1,k2], subtract pairs within one subtree, then recurse on components.
correctness: Every pair is counted at the first centroid that separates its endpoints; there its path passes through the centroid and is counted once by the depth-sum condition.
complexity: O(n log^2 n) time and O(n log n) space, depending on range-count structure.
